newsitem.title: UK: Expro Intl sees plenty growth opportunities.
newsitem.headline: Expro Intl sees plenty growth opportunities.

text.p: British oil services group Expro International Plc on Wednesday said it saw plenty of growth opportunities ahead after a strong performance last year.

Expro, which provides specialist services such as sub-sea safety products, saw earnings per share for the year to March 31 rise 20.5 percent to 21.2 pence following higher demand in its niche markets.
"To a degree, we create our own markets," chief executive John Dawson told Reuters.
The EPS growth rate, which compares with 28 percent the previous year, would have been around 24 percent if higher taxes and the exercise of share options by employees were discounted, Dawson said.

Operating profit as a percentage of sales fell to 17.3 percent from 18.0 percent because of higher development spending and the opening of new locations such as in Australia, while expanding facilities in the U.S. and Venezuela, Dawson said.
Expro International increased R&D spending last year to 2.1 million stg from 1.4 million.
The group's new product pipeline includes two downhole monitoring instruments to measure temperatures and oil production in increasingly deeper and therefore hotter wells.
"We believe there are plenty of opportunities for sustained long-term growth," Dawson said.
A major growth area is the Gulf of Mexico, where Expro International provides sub-sea services and its "Green Burner" product.
The Green Burner allows heavy crude from exploration wells in the Gulf to be burned on the spot in an environmentally friendly way, making expensive transport to shore unnecessary.
No other similar product is allowed to be used in the area, Dawson said.
Shares in Expro International rose 22-1/2 pence to 490 with 109,552 stocks having changed hands in mid-morning business.
